newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Party leader appeals for calm after Indonesia riot.
newsitem.headline: Party leader appeals for calm after Indonesia riot.

text.p: The chairman of Indonesia's Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP), Ismail Hasan Metareum, has appealed to party supporters for calm after recent riots in a Java town, newspapers reported on Saturday.

Eight people were injured during Wednesday's riots in Pekalongan, central Java, apparently sparked by reports that a popular singer, who used to be a PPP supporter, had switched allegiance to the ruling Golkar party.
Pekalongan, 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta, was the only city in central Java where Golkar lost to the PPP in the 1992 elections. The next general elections will be held on May 29.

"He (Metareum) has asked the people, especially the PPP supporters, to calm down and refrain from doing unlawful things, such as property destruction," the Moslem-oriented Republika newspaper said on Saturday.
The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted Metareum as saying his party would investigate the incident and promised to "never wash his hands" if his cadres were involved.

At least 60 shops were either burned or ransacked, two cars were set ablaze and a state-run bank was damaged during the violence in which the rioters mainly attacked the property of ethnic Chinese. Thirty-one people have been detained in connection with the incident.

Popular pop singer Rhoma Irama appeared at a ceremony organised by Golkar in Pekalongan on Tuesday along with a high-profile television Islamic preacher and President Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.

Some newspapers said the riot erupted after the organisers of the Golkar gathering had taken down the flags of the three political parties: Golkar's yellow flags, green flags of the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI)'s red flags.

The Jakarta Post said some residents believed the incident erupted because the supporters of the two minority parties were upset because their parties' colours were taken down while Golkar constructed a stage for the singer's performance draped in yellow.
